traits.note: Flora of China vol. 13 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Pereskia (the subfamily's one genus in the flora): Shrubs or climbers, or trees to 20 m tall. Branches terete, slightly fleshy when young; areoles with spines; glochids absent. Leaves somewhat fleshy, sessile or petiolate, broad, flat, pinnately veined, estipulate. Flowers solitary, or in fasciculate, subcorymbose, racemose or paniculate inflorescences, stalked or sessile. Receptacle not produced into a tube beyond ovary, with numerous, ± leafy, often persistent scales. Perianth multiseriate; segments free, spreading or rotate, white to red, magenta or orange. Stamens numerous. Fruit globose, pear-shaped, or obovoid, fleshy, with or without scattered, leaflike scales. Family key: plants terrestrial; leaves present; flowers diurnal, rotate, without elongated tube; areoles without glochids; leaves broad and flat, pinnately nerved, ± persistent; flowers solitary or in inflorescences, mostly stalked. So no glochids or sheathed spines, rotate flowers, broad entire persistent alternate leaves, woody stems.
